skills.name: Action of heat on hydrates and oxides

note.text:
Heating can change substances.
Hydrates are crystals that contain water of crystallisation. On heating they lose this water and become anhydrous:
• blue hydrated copper(II) sulphate (CuSO₄·5H₂O) → white anhydrous copper(II) sulphate (CuSO₄) + water;
• washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) loses water.
Most metal oxides do not change on heating (CaO, MgO, CuO). A few decompose:
• mercury(II) oxide (red) → mercury + oxygen: 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂.
Some change colour while hot: zinc oxide is yellow when hot and white when cold.

worked_example.problem: What do you observe when blue copper(II) sulphate crystals are heated?
steps: The water of crystallisation is driven off as steam.
The crystals turn into a white powder (anhydrous copper(II) sulphate).
worked_example.answer: Steam is given off and the blue crystals turn white.

cards.idea: Hydrates contain water of crystallisation; heating drives it off.
Most metal oxides do not change on heating; mercury(II) oxide decomposes.

pick.q: What happens to zinc oxide when it is heated?
pick.r: It turns yellow, then white again on cooling.

pick.q: Which oxide decomposes on heating to give a metal and oxygen?

right.text: Heating drives off water of crystallisation.
Zinc oxide is yellow when hot.
Mercury(II) oxide gives oxygen on heating.

wrong.text: All metal oxides decompose easily on heating.
Heating a hydrate adds more water to it.
